body_markdown:
### **Why Push Provisioning Must Be Part of Your Top-of-Wallet Strategy**


*What card issuers need to know about the digital capability that spurs activation, transaction volume, and customer satisfaction.*


For financial institutions and fintechs, the digital wallet is the new gateway to being top of wallet, and the competition for that top position is intensifying. Read on to dig into what push provisioning means for issuers today: what it is, why it matters, and how financial institutions can implement it to win primacy in their customers’ digital lives.


#### **What Is Push Provisioning?**


[Push provisioning](https://cpicardgroup.com/push-provisioning/) is the ability to load a payment card into a digital wallet — Apple Pay, Google Pay, or Samsung Pay — at the moment of card issuance, so customers can begin transacting immediately.


Traditional, or “manual,” provisioning requires the cardholder to have the plastic in hand first and manually enter the card details. Push provisioning eliminates that friction entirely, giving cardholders immediate access to a tokenized credential they can use to spend the moment their accounts are approved.


#### **Why It Matters: The Business Case**


The benefits for issuers extend well beyond customer convenience and include:


- **Top-of-wallet status from day one.** Cards provisioned to digital wallets immediately become the default payment method, driving higher activation rates.
- **Increased interchange revenue.** Customers who pay with a digital wallet transact more frequently and spend more per transaction. For the FI, that translates directly to increased interchange income.
- **Stronger cardholder stickiness.** Matching an online onboarding experience to the ability to transact immediately in a digital wallet builds lasting engagement and reduces attrition.
- **Better fraud prevention through tokenization.** Push provisioning passes an encrypted token, not the actual card number (PAN), in every transaction.[Tokens](https://cpicardgroup.com/2023/04/25/3-ways-push-provisioning-works-to-elevate-the-digital-payments-experience/) are meaningless to fraudsters and cannot be reverse engineered to expose the underlying card credential.
- **Seamless lost/stolen card recovery.** When a card is replaced, push provisioning immediately loads the new credential into the cardholder’s wallet. There is no service disruption, saving cardholders


#### **How Digital Payments Fill a Critical Gap in the Customer Journey**


Digital wallet adoption is not a future trend, it’s a present reality. 60% of issuers have expanded their secure mobile checkout options with a virtual card solution, according to[Keynova Group’s 2024 Mobile Credit Card Scorecard](https://www.keynovagroup.com/press-articles/q4-2024-mobile-credit-card) . Financial institutions trying to attract younger, digitally native customers are impatient with a seven to 10-day waiting period for a mailed card. That gap in the customer journey is precisely where push provisioning closes the loop.


“People are really looking for a seamless and frictionless interaction. As more people open accounts on their phones, there’s an opportunity for financial institutions to attract more customers,” says[Dan Molis](https://www.linkedin.com/in/danmolis/) , Director of Digital Solutions Business Development, CPI.


Molis recalled an experience he had when he signed up for a major credit card. He completed the application online but was disappointed to learn he’d have to wait up to 10 days to receive his card in the mail. That gap in the experience is where issuers risk being displaced if they do not adjust their strategies.


“We see a lot of financial institutions looking to go beyond their existing physical footprints to become more national brands,” Molis added. “Others have multiple brands and are targeting specific markets. Push provisioning is a way to provide that seamless solution and really aligns with financial institutions’ ability to grow their portfolios and create some stickiness by being top-of-wallet, both in physical and digital wallets.”


#### **Not All Push Provisioning Is the Same: How CPI’s Push Provisioning Solution Works**


CPI’s platform is processor-agnostic, integrating across the complete ecosystem of payments processors, networks, and mobile wallets. What does that mean for banks and credit unions? That you can quickly enable push provisioning with any processing or mobile app partner you choose.


#### How Push Provisioning Works


- At account opening, the cardholder receives an email, in-app or online notification inviting them to provision their card to a mobile wallet.
- The cardholder taps the “Add to X-Pay” button — CPI retrieves card credentials from the FI’s mobile app or in real time from the processor (ensuring accuracy if details have changed).
- Credentials are submitted to the appropriate token vault (Visa or Mastercard), which returns a token certificate.
- CPI delivers the token certificate back to the wallet provider that then tokenizes the card through their servers and provides that information back to Visa or Mastercard and back to the FI.
- Provisioning is complete, and the cardholder is ready to transact immediately.


#### **The Apple Mandate: Manual Provisioning Is Not Enough**


For issuers who only support manual provisioning today, Apple announced in February 2025 that it would require in-app provisioning as of January 15, 2026. The mandate was a bit of a surprise for many in the industry, but in-app provisioning provides stronger fraud protection. With manual provisioning, fraudsters could more easily provision a stolen card to their own mobile wallet.


The industry expectation is that in-app provisioning will become standard.


#### **Web Push Provisioning Offers Simple Process with a Single API Call**


Web push provisioning capabilities, currently in beta with Apple and Google Pay, enable provisioning directly from an online browser session with the wallet provider. That process uses just a single API call to CPI, which significantly reduces the integration lift and potential failure points.


In the web push provisioning scenario, the token certificate no longer has to pass through the mobile app or, in this case, the online banking portal. The token certificate is given directly to the wallet server (Apple or Google). The wallets tokenize the card and then update the associations and the issuer. Essentially one \[API\] call does it all.


#### **How Can Issuers Get Started with Push Provisioning?**


The primary prerequisite for issuers to offer push provisioning to mobile wallets is tokenization. An issuer’s BIN must be tokenized, which typically requires a project with the processor, after which CPI handles the remaining integration. CPI often participates in discussions with processors to support implementation.


Other key implementation considerations for issuers include:


- Aligning on terminology and flows early with all parties (mobile app team, processor, card networks).
- Ensuring card credentials are fully propagated to the processor before provisioning is triggered.
- Planning for a friends-and-family testing phase before production launch.
- Being mindful of the timeline; the average integration timeline is six to nine months. Existing customers with established tokenization capabilities could be up and running in as quickly as three months.


Issuers do not need to be existing CPI customers to adopt the push provisioning service.


#### **What Is the ROI for Push Provisioning?**


Key value drivers include increased transaction volume, higher activation rates, reduced inbound support calls (particularly for lost/stolen replacement), and lower card-not-present (CNP) fraud exposure through tokenization.


The compounding effect of stickier cardholders who transact more often across their entire relationship with the FI makes the ROI case compelling.


“We’re growing products and services that can grow with you as an organization,” says Molis. “We’re continually investing in and bringing innovation to our product set so you can meet your cardholders where they want to do business.”
